signals.title: AUD/NZD — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Policy Divergence
signals.text: The G10 scorecard establishes AUD as the weekly leader up +0.974% across 4 pairs while NZD trails as the laggard down -0.601% across 4 pairs, generating an extreme 1.575% bilateral spread. Macro fundamentals underline this divergence, as the RBA holds policy at 4.6% with a hiking stance while the RBNZ sits at 2.75%, granting AUD an explicit 185bp policy spread and a +337bp OIS advantage in cross carry against JPY funding. Economic momentum confirms the dispersion, evidenced by AUD's unemployment data shock beat at z=+4.04σ versus persistent data weakness in New Zealand reflected in an ESI of -17.1. Valuation metrics show AUD/NZD spot at 1.2552 trading rich against its BEER fair value of 1.2429 (z=+1.87σ), warning that the extension is stretched even as macroeconomic flow dominates. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/NZD, underpinned by the 185bp nominal rate differential and wide macroeconomic divergence. Catalyst: RBA meeting 3 Nov — hike bias priced. Risk: Spread compresses below 0.80% if commodities retrace or RBA signaling softens.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Verbal Intervention Resistance
signals.text: USD/JPY spot trades at 157.91, testing the SMA20 at 157.91 and capped beneath the SMA200 at 158.53 within a tight range-bound box. The options market displays defensive positioning, with the 1M 25d Risk Reversal printing an extreme put skew of -2.12 against an implied volatility of 7.4% and HV30 of 5.6% (VRP +1.8%). This structural demand for downside hedges sharply diverges from speculative CFTC positioning, where leveraged funds hold net short -25,598 contracts (94th percentile, z=+1.43), indicating vulnerable spec longs in USD/JPY. While Fed SOFR at 3.93% versus BoJ TONA at 1.23% preserves a +270bp OIS carry advantage in USD's favor, verbal sensitivity near 160.00 caps topside follow-through. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY on hedge-skew confirmation against crowded spec shorts. Catalyst: Fed Interest Rate Decision at 18:00 UTC followed by BoJ Interest Rate Decision at ~02:30 UTC. Risk: A confirmed break above the SMA200 at 158.53 invalidates the options hedging posture.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning Exhaustion + Volatility Risk Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1132, trapped in a clear downtrend entirely below its falling SMA20 (1.1218), SMA50 (1.1423), and SMA200 (1.1572). CFTC data shows institutional leveraged funds heavily short EUR at net -94,138 contracts, hovering at the 2nd percentile of its 52-week distribution (z=-1.72), directly diverging from retail positioning where 88% of traders sit long. Meanwhile, options markets price significant event risk ahead of central bank meetings, with 1M IV at 6.5% versus HV30 of 4.2%, creating an elevated vol risk premium of +2.4%. Rates favor the greenback via Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65% (+135bp spread), yet BEER valuation at 1.1254 marks spot as structurally undervalued at z=-2.65σ. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD with short-squeeze caution given positioning exhaustion at the 2nd percentile. Catalyst: FOMC rate decision at 18:00 UTC followed by ECB Deposit Facility decision on 29 Oct. Risk: Daily close above the SMA20 at 1.1218 confirms short covering across crowded leveraged shorts.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Yield Spread Divergence + Policy Event Risk
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4036, executing a counter-trend pullback beneath its SMA20 (1.4160) while holding above its rising SMA50 (1.4015) and SMA200 (1.3882). Leveraged funds hold CAD net short at -92,789 contracts (12th percentile, z=-1.42), maintaining bearish exposure as 4-week flows contract by -43,666 contracts. Rates firmly back USD carry, with Fed policy at 4.00% versus BoC at 2.25% delivering a +175bp nominal differential, reinforced by OIS SOFR at 3.93% over CORRA at 2.24% (+169bp). However, short-end rate momentum presents an obstacle, as the CA-US 2Y yield spread narrowed by +7bp over 5D and +19bp over 20D to -131bp, slowing upward momentum ahead of imminent central bank policy updates. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD on structural carry support above key moving averages. Catalyst: BoC Interest Rate Decision at 13:45 UTC followed by FOMC Rate Decision at 18:00 UTC. Risk: Sustained break below SMA50 support at 1.4015 accelerates the technical correction.
